name: Two-Eyed Seeing
short: Indigenous and Western knowledge, side by side.
text: A common framework of principles, targets and criteria drawing on the strengths of Indigenous and Western knowledge systems.
act: Shared governance at work. A Collaborative Research Agreement with the Squamish Nation, signed in April 2024, binds this work to the Nation's core values and to two-eyed seeing. EcoScapes is designed to complement the stewardship the Nation leads under X̱ay Temíxw, its Sacred Land Use Plan.

name: Establish functional wildlife corridors
short: Keep wildlife routes open, valley to mountaintop.
text: Identify and map wildlife corridors that enable movement for the broadest possible range of species, from valley bottoms to mountaintops.
act: Keep these routes open. Plan roads, trails and development around them, not through them.

name: Restore structural connectivity
short: Reconnect the land along its streams.
text: Target restoration on fish-bearing riparian networks and sensitive ecosystems within interconnected high-quality wildland habitat.
act: Reconnect the landscape along its streams: culverts, crossings, streamside planting.

name: Secure ecosystem functions
text: Maintain, enhance and restore ecosystem functions for their intrinsic value and the benefits they provide to people.
act: Keep the places that give us clean water, flood protection and carbon storage working, and in natural cover.

name: Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
short: Restore sensitive places where it counts most.
text: Focus restoration on the top 30% of important, environmentally sensitive areas degraded by human activity and natural processes.
act: Restore where it counts most: sensitive places that will still be buffered as the climate changes.
who: Restoration groups, land trusts, resource managers

national.text: 30% of degraded ecosystems under effective restoration

regional.indicator: Restoration potential: sensitive, degraded land with high climate buffer

name: Protect 30% of high-value habitat
short: Protect the intact, high-value places first.
text: Effectively conserve 30% of lands with high biodiversity value, and increase habitat with high adaptive capacity.
act: Protect the intact, high-value places first. The gap between these and what is already protected is the 30×30 job.
who: Planners (ESAs, OCPs), land trusts, Province, First Nations

name: Climate-informed conservation
short: Conserve places that stay liveable as it warms.
text: Increase land that will keep offering suitable habitat and buffer climate variability, so species can persist locally.
act: Conserve the places that will stay liveable as the climate shifts: cool valleys, shaded slopes, high ground.
